Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Vista Energy Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Vista Energy Holdings' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Robert Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Michael Torres, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
    2. Key achievements and challenges during the quarter.
    3. Rate base growth and factors impacting growth.
    4. Grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.
    5. Storm response and recovery efforts.
    6. O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains.
    7. Comparison of current period results to prior periods and guidance.
    8. Forward-looking statements and implications.

Let me provide some more detail on these eight key aspects. First, on regulatory rate cases, we've secured over $1.2 billion in incremental revenue authorizations year-to-date across our six-state footprint. Second, key achievements include record generation volumes and new renewables commissions, though we navigated weather headwinds and fuel cost pressures. Third, our rate base hit $28.4 billion, up nearly 7% year-over-year. Fourth, grid modernization efforts have slashed outage durations significantly. Fifth, our storm recovery was swift, restoring power to nearly all customers within days. Sixth, O&M expenses dropped over 7% through predictive tech and efficiencies. Seventh, revenues rose 12% year-over-year with strong beats on EPS and EBITDA. And eighth, we're guiding robust EPS growth into 2025 amid clean energy tailwinds.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss the financials in depth.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024 quarter, we reported adjusted diluted EPS of $1.45 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model across regulated utilities, merchant generation, and renewables, and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me start with a comparison of our current period results to prior periods and our updated guidance. Consolidated revenues reached $2.85 billion, up 12% from $2.54 billion in Q3 2023 and 8% sequentially from Q2 2024's $2.64 billion. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.12 billion, up 18% year-over-year from $950 million and 7% from Q2's $1.05 billion, driving adjusted EPS of $1.45—beating consensus by $0.08 and up 15% from $1.26 last year. Net income was $785 million, or $1.32 per share, versus $680 million or $1.18 per share in Q3 2023.

In our regulated utilities segment, serving 4.2 million customers in Georgia, the Carolinas, and Ohio, revenues were $1.65 billion, up 10% YoY from $1.50 billion, thanks to 8% rate base growth to $28 billion and 7% higher retail sales of 22.5 million MWh amid 15% above-normal cooling degree days. EBITDA margins improved to 42% from 39%, supported by $450 million in CapEx on grid hardening and 500 MW of battery storage. O&M held flat at $320 million due to digital optimizations.

Our power generation segment, with 25 GW capacity—40% gas CCGT, 25% nuclear, 20% renewables, balance coal and hydro—saw revenues of $1.05 billion, up 17% YoY from $900 million. Nuclear hit 4.2 million MWh at 93% capacity factor; renewables surged 35% to 2.8 million MWh; ERCOT gas sales averaged $48/MWh on 5.1 million MWh, capturing peaks at $250/MWh. EBITDA grew 25% to $680 million at 65% margins, aided by a new 200 MW/400 MWh BESS hybrid. Coal output fell 12% as we idle units ahead of retirements. Corporate revenues were steady at $150 million from hedging.

Free cash flow before growth CapEx was $950 million, up 14% YoY, funding our $0.72 dividend (3.8% yield) and $300 million buybacks. Liquidity is $4.2 billion; net debt/EBITDA at 3.4x.

Turning to full-year 2024 guidance, we're raising it: adjusted EBITDA to $4.45-$4.65 billion (12-16% growth over 2023's $3.98 billion), EPS $5.40-$5.70 (from $5.20-$5.50), retail sales at high end of 6-8%, renewables +30% YoY. Q4 EBITDA $1.05-$1.15 billion, EPS $1.20-$1.35. Assumptions include normal weather, PJM/ERCOT prices at $38/$45/MWh, Henry Hub $2.90/MMBtu, CapEx $2.1 billion with $800 million for 1.5 GW solar-plus-storage.

These results tie directly into our key achievements and challenges. We outperformed with adjusted EPS at $1.42 initially but beat further, revenues $3.85 billion up 7% YoY (regulated $2.1 billion up 4% from rate cases like Ohio PUCO's $150 million). Generation hit 45.5 TWh up 6%, data centers 18% of load growth (1.2 GW added), ERCOT margins $285/MWh up 22% on heat dome peaks over $10,000/MWh lambda. Renewables: 450 MW commissioned, total clean 38% capacity; SunForge 250 MW solar + 100 MW/400 MWh BESS at 92% factor, $120 million PTC/ITC; Horizon Plains II 200 MW wind 15% above P50. O&M savings $85 million via AI predictive maintenance, outages to 1.2%; $2.5 billion green bond at 4.25%. Scope 1 emissions down 14% to 1.8 million tons CO2e.

Challenges included 15% below-normal HDDs costing $110 million margins; PJM capacity $270/MW-day down 5%; gas up 11% to $4.85/MMBtu, squeezed non-hedged margins 8% (75% hedged at $3.90); CAISO curtailments 12% on 1.2 GW solar; interconnection delays 300 MW batteries; CapEx $950 million 5% over on turbine delays; coal ash $45 million; nuclear uprates 2% vs. 5%.

Now, on rate base growth: As of Q3 end, $28.4 billion, up 6.8% YoY from $26.6 billion, upper end of 6-7% CAGR. Q/Q +$450 million from $1.2 billion CapEx in service; TTM AFUDC $180 million. Drivers: T&D 55% of CapEx ($1.3 billion), e.g., MISO Badger Crossing 150 miles 345 kV ($350 million) for 800 MW wind/solar; Southeast Savannah AMI 250,000 meters, 5,000 miles hardening ($220 million), CWIP in four states at 9.75% ROE. Renewables/storage 25% ($575 million): SolarPeak 300 MW NC, 150 MW BESS IN, 5 GW pipeline. Regulatory: Ohio 10.15% ROE, Indiana 9.8%, Georgia formula 70% CWIP; net additions outpace dep 4.2x.

Headwinds: rates up AFUDC equity to 45%; supply chain delays $150 million T&D; inflation 3.2%; DER 450 MW rooftop solar. FY24 growth 6.5% to $29.1 billion; 2025-29 $12.5 billion CapEx targets 6.5-7.5% CAGR.

O&M management: Expenses $1.42 billion, down 7.2% YoY from $1.53 billion, 4.8% below guidance; non-fuel $1.12 billion down 8.5%, unplanned maint -12%, productivity +6%. 'Efficiency 2.0' $120 million invest, 4.1x ROI. Predictive: Predix APM 85% thermal fleet, 50k sensors, outages -22% to 3.3% (vs. NERC 5.1%); Liberty Creek avoided $15 million. Outages shortened 18%, heat rates 7,650 Btu/kWh +2.1% ($42 million fuel save, hedged $3.25 vs. $3.80). Workforce: 5.3% labor down, VR training, OT -24%, headcount opt 15%; procurement $68 million SAP Ariba. ERCOT drone blades -16%; PJM FERC 2222. Outlook: 6-8% further cut, $200 million FCF.

Regulatory updates: Year-to-date $1.2 billion incremental revenues toward $2.5-3 billion FY, funding 70% of $4.8 billion CapEx. PA PUCN $850 million filing: authorized $720 million (85%), 9.75% ROE (52% equity), full $1.1 billion resiliency incl ADMS/microgrids; rates +4.2% via decoupling/EE -15% kWh since 2022. NJ BPU $450 million on $300 million, 10% ROE for 1.2 GW solar/400 MW offshore; +12 cents 2025 EPS. IL ICC $650 million nuclear pending Q4, 95% path 9.8% ROE. MO PSC $320 million full 10.15% ROE $295 million for wind/EV. CA CPUC $280 million Phase 1 wildfire, 9.6% ROE, 500 MW storage. TX PUCT $180 million transmission. FERC true-up $95 million refund, Order 679 200 bps HVDC. Median ROE 9.8% up from 9.2%; 60% CapEx low-carbon; load 2.5-3% CAGR, rate base $28 billion 2026, 8-10% EPS. Filed $2.1 billion 2025 at 9.9% ROE; YTD increases 3.1% vs. sector 5%.

Our CapEx was $950 million, primarily focused on renewables and grid modernization. We remain committed to a strong balance sheet and shareholder returns, anticipating 8-10% long-term EPS growth.

Forward-looking: Adjusted EPS FY25 $5.75-$6.10 (8-12% growth), EBITDA $4.2-$4.5 billion up 10%; CapEx $5.5-$6.0 billion (60% renewables/storage: 4.2 GW 2025-27 incl 2.5 GW solar SE/ERCOT, 1.2 GW wind Midwest, 500 MW BESS); 1.1 GW hyperscaler PPAs $35-40/MWh; ERCOT 800 MW/400 MWh BESS 20% IRR. Northeast PJM $120/kW-month capacity, NY 70% RE; CA LCFS/SGIP 12-15% returns. Thermal: 1.2 GW CCGT H2-ready; SMR 200 MW ID 2029. FCF $2.8-$3.1 billion, 4.2% dividend, $1.5 billion repurchases; ROE 11.5-12% 2027, rate base $45 billion. Demand 4-6% CAGR data centers/EVs; risks rates, IRA, supply.

David Chen: Thank you, Maria. On operations, we're seeing improved efficiency in our natural gas combined-cycle power plants due to AI-driven predictive maintenance implementation. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 22%.

We've excelled in storm response. Hurricane Lila (Cat 3) and TS Marco hit Gulf/LA/MS/FL, impacting 1.2 million customers (28% base), peak 850k outages, SAIDI 12.4 hours. Mobilized 4,500 workers incl mutual aid from Duke/Entergy/Southern; IBM Maximo AI pre-trimmed 15k miles ROW -22% tree outages. Restored 65% in 12 hours, 95% 48 hours, 99.8% day 5; FL drones 80% assess +40%. Costs $460 million ($285M O&M, $175M CapEx undergrounding), 92% recoverable (60% securitization, 25% FM Global ins $350M PML, trackers). Filed $210M LA/MS, $140M ins received/$190M out, lag 4 months. Resilience program $2.5B: 50k reclosers, 200 MW BESS microgrids, elevated subs/composite poles, LiDAR 10k miles. Gulf 18% faster restore; NPS 72.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. On strategy, we're exploring battery energy storage and SMR opportunities. This will drive future growth. We're evaluating acquisitions in the ERCOT market.

Robert Kim: Thank you, Lisa. Technologically, we're investing in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We deployed Dragos platform to bolster defenses against cyber threats. We're piloting Advanced Distribution Management Systems in PJM territory.

Grid modernization details: $1.2 billion past 3 years (18% CapEx), $450M AMI/DA 2023; SAIDI -22% to 93.6 min, SAIFI -15% to 0.92, payback <5 years. AMI 2.8M meters (85% res/95% C/I) Itron/L+G, TOU 1.2M cust -14% peak, $65M DR. DA 5k reclosers/1.2k sectionalizers S&C/Eaton GE ADMS FLISR -28% CAIDI; 450 PMUs OSI PI 0.1 Hz osc detect. DER: 3.2 GW rooftop IEEE 1547, VPP 150 MW Sunrun/Tesla $12M ancillaries; $200M 500 MW BESS 2026. NE microgrids 20 MW 95% uptime; TX 2k miles hardening ABB; CA DERMS Stem AI EV 500 MW. IIJA $180M, FERC 2222 $50M; savings $85M AspenTech -40% xfmr fails. FY24 $500-600M CapEx ROIC >10%, 5-7% EBITDA grid services 2026.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, Robert. Regulatorily, we received approval for our PUCN rate case in Pennsylvania. This allows recovery of $720 million in grid resiliency investments.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Emily. Our community outreach in Gulf Coast communities resulted in a 25% increase in positive sentiment towards Vista Energy Holdings.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Maria, David, Lisa, Robert, Emily, and Michael. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for regulatory rate case execution going forward?

John Ramirez: Certainly. As Maria detailed, we've locked in strong outcomes like Pennsylvania's 9.75% ROE and 85% recovery on $850 million asked, New Jersey's accretive 10% ROE for clean mandates, Missouri's top 10.15%, and more. Pending Illinois nuclear and California wildfire keep us on track for $2.5-3 billion FY authorizations at blended 9.9% ROE for 2025 filings, funding capex while limiting bill impacts to 3.1% YTD.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: What is your outlook for rate base growth and capex allocation?

Maria Gonzalez: Great question. Rate base at $28.4 billion up 6.8% YoY, with FY24 to $29.1 billion and 6.5-7.5% CAGR through 2029 on $12.5 billion capex—55% T&D like Badger Crossing, 25% renewables as SolarPeak, 85% CapEx recovery via CWIP and cases. Tailwinds from electrification/data centers add 1-2%; risks supply chains mitigated by Siemens/GE deals.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: How are you mitigating risks related to storm events and recovery costs?

David Chen: We're proactive via $2.5 billion resilience program: reclosers, BESS microgrids, hardening, LiDAR. Lila/Marco costs $460 million fully recoverable with low lag; insurance strong, NPS steady. Faster restores than peers, diversified fleet buffers regional hits.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: What is the anticipated impact of regulatory changes on renewables integration?

Emily Vargas: Positive overall—FERC 1920/2220, state RPS like NJ 50% 2030, IRA incentives support our 4.2 GW adds. California challenges navigated via settlements; 90% settlement rate de-risks, positioning for T&D allocation on 15 GW storage needs.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Ramirez for closing remarks.

John Ramirez: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to creating long-term value for shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Vista Energy Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Vista Energy Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
